text: Do you know one ordinary metal washer left the most famous telescope ever built half blind?
This is the Hubble Space Telescope, built from NASA's own 3D model. Space Shuttle Discovery carried it up in April nineteen ninety.
Inside is a mirror two point four metres wide, polished smooth to about ten nanometres.
But the first pictures came back blurry. Something was wrong.
The edge of the mirror was too flat, by about two thousand two hundred nanometres. About one four-hundred-fiftieth of a millimetre.
Light from the edge focused in a different spot than light from the middle. It's called spherical aberration.
The cause? A testing tool on the ground had one lens out of place, by one point three millimetres.
A technician had seen a gap, and filled it with an ordinary metal washer.
In December nineteen ninety-three, astronauts flew up and installed corrective optics. Glasses, for a telescope.
And the blur was gone. Hubble went on to measure how fast the universe is expanding.
